clue.text: Proceed towards the nineteenth hole and flirt with the ladies?

definitions.meaning: in golf the nineteenth hole is the clubhouse bar, reached by completing eighteen holes, i.e. a full game on the course
to dally or be unfaithful, a phrasal verb for womanising

explanation.surface: A golfer heads for the clubhouse bar and chats up the women there.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the letters two ways: PLAY A ROUND of golf ends at the nineteenth hole (golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar), while PLAY AROUND means to flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Completing a game of golf brings you to the bar; dallying with several partners is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: I have lots of money having succeeded in jobs

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits within the word for plenty of cash, so this signals a container

parts.note: pots of money is an informal phrase for a large amount
S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wealthy person boasts of a fortune made after a career of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have' only sets the boastful scene and gives no letters; the money phrase does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Positions of employment are commonly called posts, a direct synonym for jobs.

clue.text: Find a face that's fantastic — get engaged

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, telling us the preceding three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots an amazing face in the crowd and promptly proposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being betrothed to marry is exactly what affianced means, a formal synonym.

clue.text: A rare and laborious struggle to produce a colourful display

indicators.note: the letters struggle and writhe into a new order, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Producing a vivid spectacle took an unusual amount of hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the fodder and gives no letters: A RARE plus LABORIOUS is fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights are a natural light show of shifting colours in polar skies.

clue.text: A pair of legs performing in the theatre?

parts.note: in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side
a leg of a journey is a stage of it

explanation.surface: A pair of dancer's legs high-kicking in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's leg side is also the on side, which gives ON; a leg of a journey is a STAGE. Two kinds of 'leg' make the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the boards during a show is a plain idiom for acting or performing.

clue.text: Money set aside from scrimping gets enjoyed after upturn

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn turns the extracted letters so they read bottom to top
the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Savings built up by thrift are spent happily once the economy recovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to GGETSEN in scrimpinG GETS ENjoyed; 'after upturn' turns that run upward to read NESTEGG.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings put by for the future are idiomatically a reserve fund held back, the phrase meaning exactly that.

clue.text: Work that's behind the counter

definitions.meaning: to work soil is to cultivate or plough it
the cash register a shopkeeper keeps out of customers' reach

explanation.surface: A shop assistant's job is behind the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilling is ploughing land; a cash drawer in a shop is the other sense of the same word.

clue.text: Trailing behind? To achieve victory must get last two up front

indicators.text: must get last two up front
indicators.note: the final pair of letters is shifted to the start of the word

parts.note: to win is to achieve victory

explanation.surface: A team lagging behind must get its two stragglers to the front to win.
explanation.walkthrough: TO WIN with its last two letters moved to the front gives IN TOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being towed is pulled along at the rear of a vehicle, a literal sense of trailing.

clue.text: What accounted for the brilliance of the early music halls?

definitions.text: What accounted for the brilliance of the early music halls?

parts.words: What accounted for the brilliance of the early music halls?
parts.note: brilliance hints at fame, but literally the bright stage light made by heating calcium oxide

explanation.surface: A question about why Victorian variety theatres were so glittering.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatres were once lit by heating quicklime to incandescence; that literal stage light is now the figure of speech for public attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The calcium-oxide spotlights of nineteenth-century stages are the literal origin of the word for fame.

clue.text: Not a single person exactly right for comic drama

definitions.text: Not a single person exactly right
definitions.meaning: a married man who is perfect for his wife: someone not single, and the perfect choice

explanation.surface: Finding the perfect married partner would make a funny play.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Oscar Wilde's comedy; read literally, a husband is not single and ideal means exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's society comedy carries this title; a flawless spouse is the literal reading.

clue.text: Expeditions allowing little girl to cover a great distance

indicators.note: the girl's name goes around the distance phrase, wrapping it

parts.note: sis is a short form for sister
afar means at or to a great distance

explanation.surface: A small girl is allowed to travel a long way on trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Safaris are journeys or hunting trips, especially in Africa, a fair synonym for expeditions.

clue.text: Private room is a problem with any number in performance needing to squeeze in

indicators.note: the combined piece is pushed into the middle of the problem word

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in school

indicators.note: the number letter is placed inside the performance word

parts.note: an act is a turn or performance on stage
in maths n stands for any number

explanation.surface: A private room is needed as backstage space is tight for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is an inner retreat where one is free from intrusion, such as a study.

clue.text: Celebrity carrying one piece of luggage for flight

indicators.note: the celebrity word holds the numeral inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
I is the Roman numeral one
a case is a suitcase

explanation.surface: A famous person takes a single bag on a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel to go with luggage, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, which a stairway provides.

clue.text: Peg's party, agreeably short

parts.note: a do is an informal party

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off, leaving the word short

parts.note: well, as in getting on well, means agreeably

explanation.surface: Peg's party went quite pleasantly, if briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg's' looks like a woman's name; it is the definition, with 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden pin or peg used to join pieces of timber.

clue.text: Biblical sufferer admits insomnia, finally beginning to count sheep

indicators.note: the sufferer's name lets the two letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: Job is the Old Testament figure tested by great suffering

indicators.note: takes only the closing letter of insomnia
takes only the opening letter of count

explanation.surface: A sleepless patriarch starts counting sheep to drift off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheep' looks like part of the sleep remedy, but it is the definition: the Jacob is a piebald breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacob is a spotted, multi-horned breed of domestic ovine named after the Genesis patriarch.

clue.text: Relation I caught in joke becomes most cheerful

indicators.note: the relative and the I are trapped within the joke word

parts.note: a jest is a joke
an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: A relative caught up in a prank becomes the life of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means lively and self-confident, so the superlative form means in the highest spirits.

clue.text: After end of romance it's no good ranting to create an impression

indicators.note: takes the final letter of romance

parts.note: raving means ranting wildly

explanation.surface: After a failed love affair, raging about it achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A print taken from an incised plate is an impression, as in a print run.

clue.text: Carry out a tool

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to put it into effect

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning execute and as a noun for a utensil.

clue.text: Unsporting junior employee

definitions.meaning: an ... is a subordinate worker, a hand being a labourer

explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealing is deceitful; the split form gives a lower-ranked worker.

clue.text: A short period in employment makes one severely self-disciplined

indicators.note: the shortened period goes inside the employment word

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting something to use

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped, so the word comes up short

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: Brief spells in a job make a person stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes one' is only a link; 'severely' leans toward the definition but is part of it, since severe self-discipline is the full sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes a strict, ascetic way of life, without comfort or indulgence.

clue.text: A particular female in the bar upset, in serious trouble

indicators.note: the particular-female letters sit inside the turned bar
in a down clue upset turns the word so it reads upward

parts.note: a rod is a bar
one, as in 'one woman I know', means a particular

explanation.surface: A certain woman in a pub is upset and in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a pub, but it is a rod, turned upward by 'upset' to DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done for is an idiom meaning ruined or beyond rescue.

clue.text: Go away to get success in work? The opposite

indicators.note: suggests the success goes inside the work word
reverses that instruction, so the work goes inside the success

parts.note: a hit is a success
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A command to leave, then a puzzle about succeeding on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' tells you to swap the container instruction just given: the work goes around nothing, the success goes around the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is a British imperative telling someone to leave, like scram.

clue.text: I'll leave track with a warbled expression of joy

indicators.note: the letter departs from the track word

parts.note: a trail is a track
the letter I, read from the start of the clue as 'I will'

explanation.surface: Someone singing happily as they set off on a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll leave' means the letter I will leave TRAIL, giving TRAL; then add A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a sung refrain used to show gaiety or carefree mood.

clue.text: Elite group had a snack maybe in the morning

parts.note: ate, with the snack only one example of eating
a.m. means before noon

explanation.surface: Top performers grabbed a bite before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-team is the best squad or set of people, the first-choice selection.

clue.text: Growing old, muddling sentences

indicators.note: jumbling up, so the letters of the next word are mixed

explanation.surface: An ageing person getting sentences confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent is the formal word for ageing or deteriorating with age.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic little boy, about three and a bit

indicators.note: the boy's name goes round the number

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name, a short form of Edward
pi is 3.14159..., just over three

explanation.surface: A small boy aged a bit over three seems listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm in feeling, tepid describes a half-hearted reception.

clue.text: Christian living in severe circumstances before getting money from widow?

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
the widow's mite, the tiny coin given in the Gospel story

explanation.surface: A devout ascetic takes a gift from a poor widow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mark 12 a poor widow gives two mites, all she had; the question mark flags the allusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit living alone in austere conditions.

clue.text: Narrowly ahead at the snooker table in a staged event?

definitions.text: Narrowly ahead at the snooker table
definitions.meaning: leading by a single game, a frame being one game of snooker
a set-up, a plot to make an innocent look guilty

explanation.surface: A snooker player holds a slim lead in a match that might be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker matches are counted in frames, so one frame up is just ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy to incriminate someone is a contrived event, staged like a play.

clue.text: Book not quite the best by this writer

indicators.note: the last letter is lost, so the word is not quite complete

parts.note: top means the best
the setter referring to themself as me

explanation.surface: An author admits their volume falls short of the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, weighty volume.

clue.text: Dreaded pet, injured, would be destroyed

indicators.note: damaged, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A feared animal, once hurt, would have to be put down.
explanation.definitionFit: Depredated means plundered or laid waste, close to ravaged.
